Title: Diagnosis of test `testObjectCycle`

Details:
The test `testObjectCycle` tries to verify that the `ToStringBuilder` handles object cycles correctly without going into infinite recursion.

Step-by-step diagnosis:

1. The test creates two instances of `ObjectCycle` (`a` and `b`), where `a.obj = b` and `b.obj = a`, creating a cyclic reference.
2. The `ObjectCycle.toString()` method uses `ToStringBuilder(this).append(obj).toString()` to generate the string representation. This delegates the string building logic to `ToStringBuilder`.
3. The `ToStringBuilder.append(Object obj)` method calls `style.append(buffer, null, obj, null)` to append the object's string representation to the buffer according to the configured style.
4. Inside the `ToStringBuilder.toString()` method, it either appends the null text if the object is null or calls `style.appendEnd(buffer, object)`.
5. The `ToStringStyle.appendEnd()` method removes the last field separator if necessary, appends content end to the buffer, and calls `unregister(object)`.
6. The `unregister(object)` method removes the object from the `REGISTRY` map that tracks objects currently being processed to prevent cycles.
7. The use of the `REGISTRY` map and `unregister()` suggests that the framework tries to detect cycles and avoid infinite recursion.

The failure indicates that the cycle detection or handling may not be working correctly, leading to incorrect or incomplete output when the object graph contains cycles. The cyclic references `a <-> b` cause repeated calls within `ToStringBuilder` and `ToStringStyle` methods that don't properly avoid infinite recursion or correctly represent the cycle.

This explains the failure of the test, which expects a specific output string demonstrating recognition of the cycle.

Next, it will be best to look into the code handling cycle detection and registration (probably some `register` method or cycle detection within `ToStringStyle` or `ToStringBuilder`) in order to identify why it is failing.

Suggested next methods to check:
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle.register(Object)`
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle.isRegistered(Object)`
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringBuilder.append(Object)` (already partially seen but might look more)
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringBuilder.toString()` (already partially seen but might look more)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
